answer: A memory-bound protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to allocate massive uncompressed tables. Each agent evaluates a block cipher across memory addresses held in a validation lagoon, while verifiers project access latencies through an analytical prism to confirm RAM residency. Adversaries incur scarce memory bus bandwidth and silicon storage costs per identity. However, time-memory trade-offs let attackers recompute values on demand, reducing hardware overhead.
